accepted.title: Spider-Man 2 review: Best-in-class comic-action melodrama
evidence: Developer: Insomniac Publisher : Sony Computer Entertainment Platform : PS5 Release Date: Oct. 20, 2023 ESRB Rating: T for Teen Price : $70 Links: Amazon | PlayStation Store | Official
As much as we liked 2020’s Spider-Man: Miles Morales , the game provided only minor tweaks to the successful formula established by Insomniac’s original 2018 take on everyone’s favorite wall-crawler
But we can’t say we’re too upset about this state of affairs. The basic open-world superheroics of Insomniac’s Spider-Man are so strong that this sequel can get by quite capably
Pretty much every piece of pre-release hype for Spider-Man 2 focused on how the pairing of two separate Spider-Men—Peter Parker and Miles Morales—would implicitly lead to twice as much fun.
Sure, the complementary powers of the two Spider-Men can work well together in battle, especially when the action pauses for a cinematic team takedown that utilizes both characters at once.
As far as the plot is concerned, the game tries to push a touching mentor/mentee relationship between the two Spider-Men that never really fits. A big part of the problem

Peter’s story quickly becomes entangled with that of Harry Osborne, a childhood friend who has finally recovered from a somewhat mysterious illness. Harry’s reintroduction helps solve an early mid-life crisis

Miles, meanwhile, deals with an almost completely unrelated plotline centered around his internal battle between feelings of revenge and forgiveness directed at Mr. Negative, the man who killed his father.
